content.comment_body: What does ES3 refer to? Is it simply a [product_name] module with increased functionality? Could someone explain this further?

Hello [user_name]! This is an easy question. [company_name] caused some confusion with their release of the -[article_no] version of the [product_name] module. 1) The 'Standard' [product_name] -[article_no] was released around August 2008. 2) At launch, it didn't support Japanese characters or menu text as promised, but did include support for nine other languages. 3) Japanese language support was added later in November 2008 at a technology fair. 4) This updated version is called the ES3 version (ES stands for 'Development Step' in German). 5) To identify which version you have, check your [product_name] device for a small cross and numbers; the number replaced by an 'X' indicates the E-Stand number. See the attached [document] for more details. 6) To work with these modules, you need at least [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] (with the latest service pack [version_no]), available from the official download page. 7) When selecting your target device for programming, choose 'Standard' [article_no] for E-Stand 2 or earlier, and 'ES3' for E-Stand 3 or later (E-Stand 4 was recently released, which is why the latest service pack is recommended—it brings new features and fixes). Cheers! Aaaarrggh! (Barbarian for 'Have a nice day!')

analysis.insight_summary: The conversation clarifies confusion about the meaning of 'ES3' and '-[article_no]' versions of the [product_name] module. Initially, users encountered language support limitations, particularly with Japanese, after the release of the standard model. The ES3 label was introduced with an updated module that addressed these issues, and users discuss how to identify and correctly use different versions with compatible software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a simple and detailed explanation of what ES3 stands for and how it is distinct from the standard -[article_no] [product_name] module, expecting advice on improved features and appropriate software versions for support.
